item.title: 📚 Book Club Today / 📝 New Vision Zero Report / 🏆 Announcing Our Urbanist Award Winners
item.description:
📚 BOOK CLUB TODAY

Join us TONIGHT, Wednesday, December 3rd for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action). Cheese pizza will be served for dinner.

📝 NEW VISION ZERO REPORT

This past week, the City released the Vision Zero Action Plan 2030, a new report highlighting the progress and challenges on the road to reaching zero deaths or serious injuries from traffic collisions.

🏆 ANNOUNCING OUR URBANIST AWARD WINNERS

Congrats to the winners of the 2025 Urbanist Awards!

🎖️ Urbanist Lifetime Achievement Award - Job Itzkowitz, Executive Director, Old City District
🚍 Urbanist Changemaker of the Year - Joi Washington, Mayor-Elect, Media Borough
🏛️ Public Servant of the Year - Molly Hartman, Senior Policy Director for CM Landau
🛴 Advocacy Partner of the Year - Stephen Bronskill, Coalition Manager, Transit Forward Philadelphia
🚲 Neighborhood Champion - Ashlei Tracy, President, Fishtown Neighbors Association
🏙️ Best Development of the Year - Calder Gardens
🏞️ Best Public Space Improvement of the Year - Ashley Lepera, LeCount Street Reversal Organizer
📰 Urbanist Media Champion - Alan Fisher, Armchair Urbanist Series Creator
🏆 5th Square Volunteer of the Year - Morgan Allgrove-Hodges, Transit Committee Co-Chair

Come celebrate the winners with us at our holiday party and awards ceremony on December 12th. Join us to celebrate with other Philadelphia built environment activists, neighborhood and community leaders, architects, planners, builders, and sustainability advocates at the urbanist holiday party of the season!

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏙️ Philly2050 Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is looking to hear from you about what you want for the future of the city. We encourage you to respond in support of key urbanist issues like transit-oriented housing, walkable neighborhoods, expansion of transit options, protected bike lanes, and more.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

🚲 Parking-Protected Bike Lane Petition

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal in PA! The Bicycle Coalition is fighting for their legalization. Sign their petition to show your support for safer bike lanes!

EVENTS

Book Club: When Driving Is Not an Option
Wednesday December 3rd • 5:30 pm | Bicycle Coalition 8th Floor Amenity Room, 1500 Walnut St
Join us, the Bicycle Coalition, and Philly Bike Action for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action) with pizza served for dinner.

SEPTA Holiday Bus Display
December 06, at 11:00am - 12pm | Love Park, 1501 JFK Blvd
SEPTA is hosting it’s annual Holiday Bus Display and People’s Choice Awards at Love Park. Join Transit Forward Philly as they check out the decorated buses and share ways that people can take action to support transit.

5th Square Holiday Party + Annual Urbanist Awards Ceremony
Friday, December 12th at 7 PM | Indy Hall, 709 N 2nd St
Join 5th Square members and friends for our Holiday Party + Urbanist Awards Ceremony where we will be presenting awards to members of our community for their outstanding contributions to Philadelphia’s urbanist movement.

Transit Forward Philly: December Day of Action
December 15, at 5:30pm - 7pm | 1500 Walnut, Suite 1107
Join Transit Forward Philly as they make care packages for transit workers and riders in Philly to share our gratitude for all that they do to help Philadelphians move around the region and make up our transit community.

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

  • Inquirer.com / Is a vacant lot better than a decrepit building? Inside Philly’s latest debate over aging buildings.
  • Pennsylvania Capital-Star / Pennsylvania’s home repair program left out of state budget, despite high demand
  • WSYX / Columbus expanding affordable housing options, introduces ADU guidelines
  • WHYY / New survey asks Philly residents their ‘hopes and dreams’ for the city

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

  • PhillyVoice / How PennDOT plans to install a 258-foot pedestrian bridge over Columbus Boulevard in one night
  • Inquirer.com / Elfreth’s Alley is getting a park to honor woman who saved it from demolition
  • 6abc.com / Philadelphia begins Logan Circle upgrades ahead of nation's 250th birthday

🚌 TRANSIT

  • audacy.com / SEPTA to improve real-time bus, train arrival info in the coming months
  • The Keystone Newsroom / Trump administration falsely takes credit for critical SEPTA funding

🚲 MOBILITY

  • Inquirer.com / Philly wants to set its own speed limits, and other highlights of the city’s new Vision Zero report
  • NBC10 Philadelphia / Woman struck and killed, driver attempts to flee in University City, police say
  • usa.streetsblog.org / Opinion: One Less Lane Ought To Fix It
  • The Washington Post / The deadliest roads in America

item.title: 🚉 Emergency SEPTA Funding / 📣 Support Sidewalk Cafes and Safe Streets / 🏙️ Philly2050 Survey
item.description:
🚉 EMERGENCY SEPTA FUNDING

Yesterday, Governor Shapiro announced an emergency allocation of $220 million to SEPTA for a series of critical repairs to Regional Rail, the trolley tunnel, and Metro.

We applaud this move as a step in the right direction. This represents a real down payment toward keeping the Philadelphia region moving and ensuring that the state’s economic engine continues to strengthen and support the rest of the Commonwealth.

But this cannot be where the work to support public transit in the region ends. SEPTA's operating shortfall remains an urgent concern and without closing that gap through stable, long-term funding, riders will remain at risk of service cuts, reduced frequency, service disruptions, and fare hikes.

We urge Governor Shapiro to follow through on this emergency measure with a long-term commitment that fully secures the future of public transit not just for Philadelphia, but across all of Pennsylvania.

📣 SUPPORT SIDEWALK CAFES AND SAFE STREETS

Come to City Council to comment in SUPPORT of sidewalk cafes and bills for safer streets.

City Council, Streets & Services Committee
Tuesday, December 2nd at 10 AM
Philadelphia City Hall, Room 400

  • 🍽️ #251022 - expanding by-right sidewalk cafes in Northwest, South, and West Philly!
  • 🚲 #251024 - adding the 5th Council district (Logan Square, portions of Rittenhouse Square) to the Center City loading zones bill in response to the Pine-Spruce litigation
  • 🚸 #250982 - changing the directions of LeCount and Bambrey streets near South St, in response to multiple crashes involving turning vehicles and people biking.

RSVP here and we will loop you in with our volunteers attending with talking points and register you for comment with council staff.

🏙️ PHILLY2050 SURVEY

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is looking to hear from you about what you want for the future of the city.

  • Transit-Oriented Housing
  • Dense, Walkable Neighborhoods
  • Expansion of Transit Options, including Trolley Modernization, Reimagining Regional Rail and a Subway for Roosevelt Blvd
  • A Network of Protected Bicycle Lanes
  • Repurposing City-Owned Surface Parking Lots

Give Your Input

🏆 URBANIST AWARDS NOMINATIONS DUE BY SUNDAY

Have a friend or colleague who deserves an award for their contributions to Philadelphia's urbanist movement? Nominate them for our annual urbanist awards!

Nominations are due by Sunday, December 1st at 5pm.

We will be presenting awards to the winners at our holiday party on December 12th. Join us to celebrate with other Philadelphia built environment activists, neighborhood and community leaders, architects, planners, builders, and sustainability advocates at the urbanist holiday party of the season!

Get your tickets today!

📚 BOOK CLUB: WHEN DRIVING IS NOT AN OPTION

Join us next week on Wednesday, December 3rd for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action). Cheese pizza will be served for dinner.

Anna Zivarts is a disability justice advocate, a low-vision parent, and the founder of the Week Without Driving. She draws attention to the fact that 1/3rd of Americans do not have a driver’s license and says that our transportation systems must be inclusive of EVERYONE–not just people who drive cars. 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE ADVOCACY IN THE NEWS

Inquirer.com / West Philly affordable housing project could finally advance, almost 6 years after it was proposed

“It’s a travesty that one deep-pocketed opponent has been able to block access to housing for over 100 families in my neighborhood for years,” said Will Tung, a neighbor of the project and a volunteer with the urbanist advocacy group 5th Square. “It’s more expensive than ever to rent or buy here, and this project would be a welcome change to its current use as a derelict warehouse.”

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here.

🚲 Parking-Protected Bike Lane Petition

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal in PA! The Bicycle Coalition is fighting for their legalization. Sign their petition to show your support for safer bike lanes!

Join us, the Bicycle Coalition, and Philly Bike Action for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action) with pizza served for dinner.

Join Pro-Housing Philly for their December meeting, featuring guest speakers Senator Nikil Saval and Rep. Tarik Khan. They will discuss the Harrisburg politics of housing reform and talk with the reps about the housing bills they're working on at the state level.

item.title: 🏙️ A Better Market East / 🚵‍♀️ Tomorrow: Spring Garden Connector Open House / 🚇 Thursday: Transit Affordability Townhall
item.description:
🏙️ A BETTER MARKET EAST

Ask for a more walkable, vibrant and dense Market East.

The City is leading an effort to revitalize Market Street, from Broad Street to the Delaware River -- and is soliciting public input.

Suggested comments:

Traffic & Transportation:

  • Prioritize roadway safety & bus users-- install curb bump-outs, raised & protected bike lanes, and prioritize bus lanes.
  • Remove one eastbound car travel lane to give space to people walking and biking.
  • Discourage curb cuts and parking decks to encourage transit use and preserve walkability.

Vacant property and open space:

  • Prioritize housing units, both affordable and market rate, to provide a stable year-round customer base for area stores and businesses.

Retail and shopping:

  • Promote ground level retail and neighborhood services, with storefronts of varying sizes and doors that open on to the street to enhance safety and walkability.
